judged_text: parseRefreshTokenResponse overwrites a missing refresh_token in the parsed data with the literal string "refresh_token", and consumers spread that parsed data into the stored credential (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:263 spreads tokenResponse.data over o365AuthCredentials). The user's real refresh token is permanently replaced by the literal "refresh_token" in the credential row, so any later refresh that does not go through the sync endpoint (sharing disabled, sync endpoint unset, or parent app down) sends refresh_token=refresh_token to the provider and fails with invalid_grant — the integration cannot recover without re-auth.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, if the parsed token response lacks `refresh_token`, the function mutates the parsed `.data` by setting `refresh_token` to the literal string "refresh_token". Callers then merge/spread the parsed `.data` into persisted credential objects. For example in `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }` will overwrite the existing real `refresh_token` with that literal when the refresh response doesn’t include a refresh token (a common OAuth behavior). This permanently corrupts the stored credential’s refresh token, causing subsequent refreshes that rely on the stored value to fail.
